newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arafat says "no progress" in Hebron talks.
newsitem.headline: Arafat says "no progress" in Hebron talks.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat said on Friday intensive negotiations with Israel on a long-delayed troop redeployment in the West Bank town of Hebron had failed to make headway.

"Unfortunately there is still no progress," Arafat told reporters before inaugurating a housing project in self-ruled Gaza. He said he hoped a deal that would clear the way for Israel to transfer most of Hebron to Palestinian control would soon be clinched but that "big differences" remained.

Palestinian and Israeli negotiators failed in overnight talks to break an impasse over Israel's demand its troops be allowed to enter PLO-run areas in Hebron, where 400 Jews live and study amidst 100,000 Arabs, in "hot pursuit" of suspected guerrillas.
"The Israelis' insistence to have the right to re-enter areas handed over to the Palestinians led to disagreements," Palestinian negotiator Major-General Abdel Razak al-Yahya told Reuters.
Israeli government spokesman Moshe Fogel acknowledged talks remained snagged: "There is no change."
Yahya said talks would resume on Sunday.

Israel has completed many of the security arrangements to transfer 80 percent of Hebron to Palestinian rule. But Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu wants to modify the Hebron accord signed by the centre-left government he ousted last May to bolster safeguards for Jewish settlers in the volatile town.
Palestinians reject any alterations of the signed accord.
